title: Pinned simultaneous-bucket second-trace differences have minimum nonzero-Gauss rank at least four
statement: For every distinct squarefree degree-eleven pair in one simultaneous coefficient/inverse bucket at (ell,d)=(9,8), if the Gauss sum of the second-trace difference is nonzero then its polar rank is at least four. THIS PROPOSITION IS FALSE: five pairs have phase-trivial radical and polar rank two.

evidence.supports: The exact 683-form table partitions all 28,830 unordered within-bucket pairs into ten rank/radical types and finds five nonzero quadratic Gauss sums of polar rank two.
evidence.notes: The checker computes nullspaces over GF(2) and independently sums every quadratic truth table; the five polynomial differences are pinned.

provenance.source: native exact second-trace quadratic forms and binary linear algebra

notes: This refutes a precise finite high-rank premise and stops the raw Kerdock model. It does not exclude cancellation after signed aggregation across buckets or orders and grants no endpoint credit.
